question.worked_solution:
The integral is defined over a type II region $D=\{(x,y)\,:\,0\le y\le \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2},\,y\le x\le \sqrt{1-{y}^{2}}\}.$

So, we can express the integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}x(1-y)\,dA & ={\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{2}/2}{\int }_{y}^{\sqrt{1-{y}^{2}}}x(1-y)\,dx\,dy\end{aligned}
$$

First, we evaluate the inner integral by integrating with respect to $x$, treating $y$ as a constant:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{2}/2}{\int }_{y}^{\sqrt{1-{y}^{2}}}x(1-y)\,dx\,dy & ={\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{2}/2}(1-y)[{\int }_{y}^{\sqrt{1-{y}^{2}}}x\,dx]\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{2}/2}(1-y){[\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}]}_{y}^{\sqrt{1-{y}^{2}}}\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{2}/2}(1-y)(\frac{1-{y}^{2}}{2}-\frac{{y}^{2}}{2})\,dy \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{2}/2}(1-y)(1-2{y}^{2})\,dy \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{2}/2}(1-y-2{y}^{2}+2{y}^{3})\,dy\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we integrate with respect to $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{2}/2}(1-y-2{y}^{2}+2{y}^{3})\,dy & =\frac{1}{2}{[y-\frac{{y}^{2}}{2}-\frac{2}{3}{y}^{3}+\frac{1}{2}{y}^{4}]}_{0}^{\sqrt{2}/2} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}-\frac{1}{4}-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{6}+\frac{1}{8}-0) \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{2}}{6}-\frac{1}{16}\end{aligned}
$$
